Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

repeat verb

say or do again

also say again, say that again, repeat after me, do again, repetition

classical

Cic. Att. 14.14.1: Iterādum eadem ista mihi.
Liv. 1.45.2 (Lewis & Short): saepe iterandō eadem

iterō, iterāre, iterāvī, iterātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

say or do a second time, repeat

From iterum, “a second time”: to say the same words again, or do a thing again (pugnam iterāre, Liv. 6.32). In farming it is to plough a second time (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • repetō, repetere, repetīvī, repetītum — go over again, repeat; resume

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Traupman 34: repete quid modo dīxerīs, repeat what you just said; Cic. Fin. 5.51 (Lewis & Short): praetermissa repetimus

    To go back over what was said or begun, so also to resume; Traupman’s classroom word. Its first senses are to attack again and to go back for, fetch, or claim back (rēs repetere); Lewis & Short.

  • dīcō iterum (rūrsus) — say again

    phrase · also used · classical

    The plain way: Dīc iterum, say it again. Traupman 34 has eīsdem verbīs mihi redde for “repeat after me”.

Examples

  • Iterādum eadem ista mihi.

    Say that to me again!Cic. Att. 14.14.1

  • repete quid modo dīxerīs

    repeat what you just saidTraupman 34

See also again, chant, every so often, say.
